POST /hosts/check.notes: operator health sweep across hosts; no journey calls it

POST /instance/{job_id}/requeue.notes: retry_instance calls /api/v1/instances/{job_id}/retry, not this. Whether the two are one authority or two is worth settling before a tool points here.

POST /instances/{job_id}/auto-launch/rep.notes: worker-agent callback reporting instance state back to the platform; authenticated as the fleet, never an agent

POST /instances/{job_id}/expose.notes: P2's launch-to-connected journey needs these; scoped for instances:connect in 406c0a1 but no tool reaches them yet

POST /instances/{job_id}/http-ports/repo.notes: worker-agent callback reporting instance state back to the platform; authenticated as the fleet, never an agent

POST /instances/{job_id}/lock.notes: Marks an instance protected from accidental modification. Precisely the guard a user would want *because* an agent can now cancel and terminate.

POST /instances/{job_id}/reset.notes: Restarts the container in place — the middle option between 'do nothing' and cancel_instance, which ends the run and loses uncheckpointed work.

POST /instances/{job_id}/restart.notes: stop/start/restart preserve the container, which is the lifecycle the platform chose over pause/resume; no tool reaches them, so an agent can only cancel or terminate

POST /instances/{job_id}/snapshot.notes: P7 commits a configured instance to a reusable image; this is that step and no tool reaches it

POST /instances/{job_id}/start.notes: stop/start/restart preserve the container, which is the lifecycle the platform chose over pause/resume; no tool reaches them, so an agent can only cancel or terminate

POST /instances/{job_id}/stop.notes: stop/start/restart preserve the container, which is the lifecycle the platform chose over pause/resume; no tool reaches them, so an agent can only cancel or terminate

POST /instances/{job_id}/unlock.notes: The release half of the lock above.

POST /marketplace/bill/{job_id}.notes: billing sweep over a completed job; the scheduler calls it

POST /marketplace/list.notes: Provider axis. Listing an admitted rig for sale is the provider's core write and is unreachable.

POST /ssh/keygen.notes: the platform's own host keypair. The public half is deliberately open because its purpose is to be pasted into authorized_keys; generating it is admin-only (see ae292c6). Never a tenant capability

POST /token/generate.notes: operator configuration — alert thresholds, the NFS mount, API token minting. Admin console, not the tool surface. The two alert paths are aliases of one handler

POST /user-images/{image_id}/complete.notes: worker-agent callback reporting instance state back to the platform; authenticated as the fleet, never an agent

POST /v1/inference.notes: Synchronous OpenAI-compatible inference, distinct from the endpoint-based serverless path run_serverless_job covers. An agent cannot use the compatible surface the API advertises.

POST /v1/inference/async.notes: The async half of the same direct-inference surface, returning a job_id.

POST /v1/serverless/{endpoint_id}/cancel.notes: stops a running serverless job. cancel_instance covers GPU instances; nothing covers this.

POST /v1/serverless/{endpoint_id}/openai.notes: an OpenAI-protocol shim over the same capability run_serverless_job already reaches. It exists so an OpenAI SDK can be pointed at the endpoint, which is a client-compatibility surface rather than a tool one.

POST /v1/serverless/{endpoint_id}/runsyn.notes: the synchronous variant of run: it blocks for the result instead of returning a job id. Different behaviour, not a second spelling, and no tool reaches it.

POST /v1/serverless/{endpoint_id}/{endpo.notes: stops a running serverless job. cancel_instance covers GPU instances; nothing covers this.
